authentication: API key as the `key` query parameter (free signup)
cost_notes: Free with a free API key.
free_tier: free API key; no paid tier documented for this API
historical_coverage: 1992 onward for the HS time series (varies by dataset)
known_limitations: PROBED 2026-11-09 WITHOUT a key: the endpoint returned HTTP 200 with an HTML page titled 'Missing Key' (8.8 KB), not JSON, not 401/403. A naive `if response.ok` client would parse an error page as data - this is the key operational trap of this source.
A DEMO_KEY attempt also returned the HTML Missing Key page, so the demo key is not a usable workaround.
Data is HS-code aggregate by country: no company, no shipment, no product identity.
Monthly values are revised after first release; the API exposes no revision timestamp, so 'known at' claims cannot be reconstructed.

Country-level HS-code AGGREGATE statistics only: no company, no shipment, no product identity. Must not be substituted for bill-of-lading (company-level) data, and cannot be used to infer any of the five firms' supply chain.
rate_limits: documented per-key query cap (Census API); keyless calls are refused
research_value: The authoritative US monthly goods trade series by HS code, useful as the US macro backdrop for device HS codes and for reconciling against Comtrade. It is aggregate only; it cannot identify any of the five firms and must never be used as a firm-level signal.
source_name: US Census Bureau International Trade API
timestamp_fields: time=YYYY-MM or YEAR/MONTH -> month/year precision only (coarse)
no publication timestamp in the API -> first-release lag and revisions are invisible
